channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: Building a Game-Based Learning Module for UK Schools: A Pre-Production Checklist
item.description: A school learning game succeeds or fails on choices made long before development starts — this pre-production checklist walks through fitting fixed lessons, shared devices and a set curriculum around them.

item.title: Hydrilla tutorial: your first BlueFox prop, from prompt to engine
item.description: A step-by-step walkthrough of generating a background prop with Hydrilla's BlueFox 1 from a prompt or reference image, complete with segmented mesh, UVs and PBR maps, while spending generation credits wisely.

item.title: Mesh Topology for Game Assets: A Pre-Export Review Workflow
item.description: A model can look fine in a still render yet pinch at joints or shade oddly in-engine, so the author lays out a pre-export topology review ordered by what each asset has to do.

item.title: Engine-Ready Texture Maps From One Photo: A Checklist for Unreal, Unity and Godot
item.description: One photo is enough to start, but engines want a full set of normal, height, roughness and AO maps — this checklist shows how to produce all four without the usual pitfalls.

item.title: A Unity Performance Pass for Mid-Range Phones: An Eight-Point Review
item.description: A Unity performance checklist for mid-range phones — eight checkpoints to keep frame rates and retention steady on older devices.

item.title: After Such a Long Wait, What's Different About the Official DLSS 5 Update for Where Winds Meet
item.description: Where Winds Meet is finally getting its official DLSS 5 build — a look at what it improves over the community workarounds players have been using.

item.title: Why Japanese text turns into tofu boxes only in packaged Unreal Engine 5 builds
item.description: Japanese text that renders fine in the editor turns into tofu boxes in packaged UE5 builds — a solo dev in Japan traces the font issue to its root.

item.title: Why Xiaomi's Concept Supercar Seeks Realism in Games
item.description: An interview with Xiaomi's car design chief on how its concept supercar chases realism inside Gran Turismo 7's Vision GT programme, a useful reference for developers working on vehicles and brand crossovers.

item.title: Hot Five: GTA 6's blockbuster launch, layoffs at Jam City, and Google Play's Best of Play 2026 winners
item.description: The week's biggest mobile stories: GTA 6's blockbuster launch, layoffs at Jam City, and Google Play's Best of Play 2026 winners.

item.title: GTA 6 generates $3.79bn in day one sales to become the biggest entertainment launch in history
item.description: Take-Two confirmed GTA 6 generated $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales, making it the biggest entertainment launch in history.

item.title: Epic Games will abandon blueprints right at the launch of Unreal Engine 6
item.description: Epic has revised its Unreal Engine 6 plans: even early versions will drop Blueprints and the Actor Gameplay Framework — a big shift for teams built on visual scripting.

item.title: Procedural Unity Tool Creates Venom-Like Tendrils That Wrap Around Any Object
item.description: This procedural Unity tool generates Venom-like tendrils that wrap around any object, offering five visual styles for developers adding organic motion to their scenes.

item.title: US mobile game spending falls to lowest of the year on GTA 6 launch day
item.description: GTA 6's launch day saw US mobile game spending fall to $28.4m, the lowest single day of 2026 by AppMagic estimates, with seven-day net revenue down 19.5% year-on-year.

item.title: Play As Puppies & Rescue Your Owner From Haunted Mansion In This Co-Op Game
item.description: LazyFlock talks through building this co-op game about puppies rescuing their owner, from custom tools to multiplayer challenges — useful reading for teams planning co-op play.

item.title: From pixel art tiles to a Godot 4 level: three workflows compared
item.description: Drawing the tileset is the fun part — turning it into a working Godot 4 TileSet is the chore, so the author compares three workflows for building a level from pixel art tiles.

item.title: Aseprite, Piskel, Pixelorama or a browser editor? Picking a pixel art tool for a small game
item.description: Instead of answering "which pixel art editor?" with a single name, the author matches Aseprite, Piskel, Pixelorama and browser editors to what you are making and where you work.

item.title: Over 25 Unreal Engine games nominated at The Game Awards 2026
item.description: From Phantom Blade Zero to Meccha Chameleon, a look at the 25-plus Unreal Engine games nominated at The Game Awards 2026.

item.title: O3DE 26.10 Released
item.description: The open-source AAA-style game engine O3DE, descended from Amazon's Lumberyard, ships version 26.10 with tooling for Windows and Linux.

item.title: How to start strong in Crownfall: Kingdoms (beginner guide)
item.description: The developer's own beginner guide to Crownfall: Kingdoms, explaining how the opening works from the actual systems, with no invented optimal build order.

item.title: Epic Games no longer plans to include Blueprints or Actor Gameplay Framework in Unreal Engine 6
item.description: Epic has changed course: Unreal Engine 6 will drop Blueprints and the Actor Gameplay Framework from day one in favor of AI-driven tooling, so developers used to visual scripting should start planning their migration now.
